purpose: Editorial definitions and FFmpeg execution guidance for cuts, transitions, timing, reframing, layering, and audio treatments.
globalRules: Choose cuts for story and action continuity before adding transitions.
Use hard cuts by default; use a transition only when it communicates time, place, energy, or a deliberate visual relationship.
Normalize resolution, frame rate, timebase, sample aspect ratio, pixel format, and audio format before concat or xfade operations.
Reset trimmed stream timestamps with setpts=PTS-STARTPTS and asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS.
Render beat-synchronized edits with accurate decoded cuts rather than keyframe-limited stream copy.
Preserve dialogue and complete meaningful action even when that requires moving a cut away from a beat.

normalizationTemplate.note: Replace W, H, and FPS per delivery profile. Subject-aware crop coordinates should replace blind center cropping when composition requires it.

techniques.name: Hard Cut
techniques.description: One shot ends and the next begins with no overlap. This is the default edit and usually the strongest choice for rhythm, action, and clarity.
useWhen: landing on a beat or onset
avoidWhen: the change should feel like a large passage of time
two static compositions clash without narrative intent

ffmpeg.implementation: Trim normalized clips at frame-accurate times, reset timestamps, then concatenate.

techniques.name: Jump Cut
techniques.description: A discontinuous cut within the same framing or action that visibly advances time. It can create urgency or remove dead speech.
avoidWhen: natural performance is more important than speed
editorialChecks: cover distracting jumps with B-roll when possible

ffmpeg.implementation: Create multiple non-contiguous ranges from one source and concatenate them; independently preserve room tone if speech gaps sound unnatural.

techniques.name: J-cut
techniques.description: Audio from the incoming scene begins before its picture appears, pulling the viewer into the next moment.
useWhen: introducing a speaker before showing them
avoidWhen: incoming audio spoils a visual reveal
audio sources would be spatially confusing

ffmpeg.implementation: Place the incoming audio earlier than its video on the timeline. This is a timeline relationship, not a single FFmpeg filter.

techniques.name: L-cut
techniques.description: Audio from the outgoing scene continues after the next picture begins, preserving thought or atmosphere across the visual cut.
useWhen: showing B-roll while a speaker finishes
avoidWhen: old audio contradicts the new location
editorialChecks: new visual supports the continuing audio

ffmpeg.implementation: Extend outgoing audio beyond its video edit and mix it beneath the incoming picture/audio as needed.

techniques.name: Match Cut
techniques.description: A cut connecting shots through similar motion, shape, composition, color, meaning, or sound.
avoidWhen: matching motion reverses screen direction unintentionally

ffmpeg.implementation: Semantic or motion-aware analysis chooses the shots and cut frame; FFmpeg executes the trims and optional reframing.

techniques.name: Montage
techniques.description: A designed sequence of short shots that compresses time, summarizes activity, or builds emotion through accumulation.
avoidWhen: the viewer needs continuous procedural understanding
every shot repeats the same information

ffmpeg.implementation: Generate a cut plan first, normalize each segment, then construct a concat/xfade graph.

techniques.name: B-roll Layering
techniques.description: Supporting footage replaces or overlays the primary image while primary speech or scene audio continues.
avoidWhen: the speaker's expression carries the moment
editorialChecks: each B-roll shot maps to the active phrase
return to the speaker for emotional emphasis

ffmpeg.implementation: Use replacement video segments with continuing primary audio, or overlay only when picture-in-picture is intentional.

techniques.name: Cross-dissolve
techniques.description: Outgoing and incoming shots overlap gradually, suggesting a softer connection, passage of time, reflection, or change of place.
avoidWhen: high-detail shots produce a muddy overlap
a hard cut would be clearer
editorialChecks: overlap does not create an accidental double subject
transition lands within a musical phrase

ffmpeg.constraint: Both video inputs must use constant frame rate and match resolution, pixel format, frame rate, and timebase.

techniques.name: Fade to Black
techniques.description: The image fades to black to close a section, mark a major break, or provide finality.
avoidWhen: used repeatedly inside a fast reel
editorialChecks: black duration is not accidental dead time

techniques.name: Whip-pan Transition
techniques.description: A rapid directional blur connects outgoing and incoming shots with compatible movement.
useWhen: matching left-right or up-down camera motion
avoidWhen: both shots are static without a motivated direction
editorialChecks: incoming subject remains readable after transition

ffmpeg.implementation: Compose directional movement and motion blur around the cut. A slide xfade alone is only an approximation; test the complete graph visually.

techniques.name: Zoom Punch
techniques.description: A brief scale change emphasizes a beat, statement, reaction, or transition.
avoidWhen: subject moves out of the crop
editorialChecks: return or cut at a deliberate event

ffmpeg.implementation: Animate scale/crop around a subject anchor; use short duration and restrained magnitude.

techniques.name: Glitch Transition
techniques.description: Brief channel offsets, displacement, frame repetition, or pixel disruption create a digital interruption.
avoidWhen: effect lasts long enough to obscure content
editorialChecks: effect aligns with a strong onset

ffmpeg.implementation: Compose a short effect segment. No single filter defines a complete glitch transition.

techniques.name: Light-leak Transition
techniques.description: A bright organic overlay briefly washes the frame to connect scenes with a nostalgic or sunlit feeling.

ffmpeg.implementation: Blend a licensed light-leak video or generated gradient over both sides of the cut; animate opacity with fade.

techniques.name: Speed Ramp
techniques.description: Playback speed changes over an action, commonly accelerating into motion and returning to normal or slow speed near a reveal.
avoidWhen: motion lacks a clean start and end
editorialChecks: speed change does not hide important action
source audio is replaced or redesigned

ffmpeg.implementation: Split the action into segments, apply different setpts factors, and concatenate. Redesign source audio or chain atempo filters within supported ranges. Use interpolation only after visual testing.

techniques.name: Slow Motion
techniques.description: An action plays below real-time speed to reveal detail, weight, or emotion.
useWhen: source was captured at high frame rate
water, food, vehicle, gesture, reaction, or impact detail
brief contrast after a fast run
avoidWhen: nothing meaningful changes in the shot
editorialChecks: source frame rate supports target speed
duration does not stall the story

ffmpeg.implementation: Prefer native high-frame-rate frames. minterpolate can synthesize frames but may fail around occlusion, spokes, water, and rapid camera motion.

techniques.name: Freeze Frame
techniques.description: A selected frame is held to emphasize a reveal, label a person/place, create comedy, or provide reading time.
editorialChecks: hold length fits text and rhythm

techniques.name: Aspect-ratio Reframing
techniques.description: A source shot is recomposed for a different canvas while keeping its important subject, motion, and text visible.
editorialChecks: face and action stay inside frame
captions and UI avoid edge zones

ffmpeg.implementation: Subject detection or human review supplies crop anchors. A blurred background fill is a fallback, not the default.

techniques.name: Split Screen
techniques.description: Two or more synchronized views share the frame for comparison, reaction, or simultaneous context.
avoidWhen: content becomes too small on mobile

ffmpeg.implementation: Normalize panel dimensions and duration before stacking.

techniques.name: Music Ducking
techniques.description: Music level is reduced dynamically when dialogue or another priority signal is present.

ffmpeg.implementation: Tune from real tracks and voices; parameter values cannot be universal. Normalize final loudness after relative mixing.

techniques.name: Audio Impact Accent
techniques.description: A short impact, whoosh, riser, engine, or natural transient reinforces a specific visual event.
avoidWhen: effect duplicates an already strong natural sound
editorialChecks: transient aligns to the visual frame
low frequencies do not clip the mix

ffmpeg.implementation: Place the effect by timestamp, trim and fade boundaries, then mix and limit.

verifiedFacts: availability and purpose of trim, setpts, concat, xfade, acrossfade, crop, scale, pad, zoompan, minterpolate, tpad, lut3d, sidechaincompress, amix, and loudnorm filters
